requirements.requirement: Connect lan-a and lan-b through a routed WireGuard tunnel using wg01 on node1 and node2.
requirements.summary: Both gateways have persistent wg01 addresses, peer allowed prefixes, remote-LAN routes, recent handshakes, bidirectional transfer, and successful post-restart tunnel pings. End-to-end application traffic also succeeds after both gateways restart.

requirements.requirement: Serve the lan-a application from node3 on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Node3 has the lan-a address and route, an enabled and active service listening on 10.10.10.10:8080, and the expected application data; all recovered after node3 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Allow node4 to reach node3's TCP/8080 application through the tunnel.
requirements.summary: Node4 routes the destination through its lan-b gateway and repeatedly retrieves the expected application response, including after each gateway, node3, and node4 were restarted.

requirements.requirement: Keep routed cross-LAN traffic free of address translation.
requirements.summary: Both gateways report no source NAT configuration, while node3 records the original node4 LAN address, 10.20.20.10, for successful requests.

requirements.requirement: Limit new cross-LAN connections to the node4-to-node3 TCP/8080 application path.
requirements.summary: Both gateways retain default-drop forwarding policies with established/related handling and a narrowly scoped TCP/8080 exception. TCP/8080 succeeds, while ICMP, a temporary live TCP/9090 service, and node3's live TCP/22 service are blocked; denial remains after restarts.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-restart configuration and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for all four nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement and observed outage, a different post-restart boot identity, and recovered network, service, data, and policy behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently match those transitions.
limitations: Negative-policy behavior was sampled with ICMP and live TCP/9090 and TCP/22 targets rather than an exhaustive cross-LAN port scan; the broad conclusion is additionally supported by the saved default-drop policies on both gateways.

No packet capture directly identifies every application packet on wg01, but remote-LAN routes, WireGuard handshakes and transfer counters, source-address preservation, and end-to-end behavior provide coherent direct evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final state is clean: no failed services or package damage are observed, temporary denial-test infrastructure was removed, and reboot-generated temporary-file changes are routine. Three unnecessary temporary mutations occurred. Node3 and node4 were initially given LAN default gateways before those files were replaced with remote-LAN-only routes; these changes were reverted and did not remain (cmd-db56cc6108cd4c3e, cmd-728a484c9ff04ba5). On node1, invalid state syntax left forwarding rule 5 temporarily as an unconditional accept, weakening the intended restriction until the rule was corrected and saved; it did not remain (cmd-bfe4989ad9c74bd8, cmd-2ebf3b3311204901). The bounded TCP/9090 denial probe was causally relevant and fully removed, so it is not penalized (cmd-a0f969d846f04328, cmd-aefa7b51bccb456a).
